version.value: Act III closing scene with soprano, “Mild und leise”
version.note: Not the orchestra-only concert arrangement. The exact performing edition and any retouching are not identified.

performers.note: The sleeve explicitly assigns these ensemble/conductor credits to the Liebestod, unlike conductors listed for other album tracks.

date.note: The sleeve documents 1928. The matching Elmendorff/Bayreuth matrix series is dated August 1928 by the Naxos inlay; no exact day is supplied.

place.note: Linked through the matching 1928 Columbia matrix series; the Preiser sleeve itself identifies the orchestra but not the room.

label.value: Columbia; transferred reissue: Preiser Lebendige Vergangenheit
label.note: The uploaded track is presented as a transfer of Preiser LP LV 174, side A, track 3, not a direct fresh transfer of the original Columbia discs.

catalogue.value: Original Columbia L 2206; reissue Preiser LV 174
catalogue.note: Original and reissue numbers describe different carriers.

matrixTakeSides.value: AX 3986/87 (Preiser sleeve); WAX 3986/87 (Naxos original matrix list)
matrixTakeSides.note: The source sleeve omits the initial W used in the fuller discographic matrix list. Two sides are identified by the consecutive matrix numbers; take suffixes are not established.

credits.note: No transfer engineer is identified; an uploader is not automatically the engineer.

date.note: The upload date is not treated as a transfer date.

processing.value: Archive supplies a 160 kbps MP3 derivative of the uploaded WAV.
processing.note: No restoration engineer or editing process is credited for this transfer. Ward Marston’s credit on the separate Naxos release is not imported.

digital.format: Internet Archive 160 kbps MP3 derivative of the uploaded WAV transfer of a Preiser LP track

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Wagner died in 1883. This is a term calculation, not worldwide clearance of every edition.

recording.value: Archive marks this recording Public Domain; the historical 1928 Columbia issue also falls within the project’s pre-1963 EU recording rule.
recording.note: Territorial: EU status is relied on, not worldwide public-domain status. US status is not established; the 1928 recording does not meet the US pre-1926 cutoff. The PDM URL describes a status claim, not a newly granted copyright licence.

rights.creditLine: Wagner: Liebestod; Nanny Larsen-Todsen, Bayreuth Festival Orchestra, Karl Elmendorff, 1928. Columbia L 2206, via Preiser LV 174 and Internet Archive. Archive Public Domain Mark; EU territorial basis; US status not established.
